report_meta.supply_chain_link: Teradyne is a back-end EQUIPMENT node — it makes the automated test equipment (ATE) that TESTS the chips after they are manufactured, sitting alongside the front-end tool makers (ASML for lithography; Applied Materials/Lam/KLA/TEL) but at the test step. Its 'wafer to AI data center' strategy means it tests almost everything in this graph: AI compute/SoC (NVIDIA GPUs and hyperscaler/Broadcom/Marvell custom ASICs), HBM/DRAM memory (Micron, SK Hynix, Samsung — see reports/Micron.json), and networking — plus it now tests server boards (Omnyx) and silicon photonics / co-packaged optics (the new Photon 100, which tests the CPO/optics that AAOI/Lumentum/Coherent build). It is one half of the global test DUOPOLY with Japan's Advantest (the leader, especially in SoC/HBM). Customers are the 'verticalized' giants: foundries (TSMC), OSATs (Amkor, ASE — see their reports), memory makers and hyperscalers. It also owns a Robotics business (Universal Robots cobots, MiR mobile robots) increasingly used in AI data centers and physical AI. Litmus test: does its stock benefit from AI being built? YES — every AI chip must be tested, and test intensity rises with complexity (HBM stacks, advanced packaging, CPO).

beginner_glossary.Teradyne: A US company that makes the machines used to TEST computer chips after they are built (plus a smaller industrial-robotics business). Every advanced chip — AI GPUs, HBM memory, networking — must be tested to make sure it works; Teradyne and Japan's Advantest dominate that test-equipment market.
beginner_glossary.ATE (automated test equipment): The big machines that automatically test thousands of finished chips for speed, function and defects. Selling ATE is Teradyne's core business. It is capital equipment — chipmakers and their packaging partners (OSATs) buy it to ramp production.
beginner_glossary.Semiconductor Test (SoC / Memory / IST): Teradyne's biggest segment. 'SoC' tests logic/compute chips (AI GPUs, CPUs, ASICs, mobile); 'Memory' tests DRAM/HBM/flash; 'IST' (formerly system-level/HDD test) tests drives and at the system level. In Q1 2026 Semi Test broke $1B in a quarter for the first time.
beginner_glossary.SoC test (system-on-chip): Testing complex logic chips. Teradyne's UltraFLEXplus is its flagship SoC tester. Compute (AI) is now ~75% of its SoC revenue — the business has shifted from mobile-centric to AI-dominant.
beginner_glossary.Memory / HBM test: Testing memory chips, especially the AI-critical HBM (stacked high-bandwidth memory) and DRAM. Teradyne's Magnum platform competes with Advantest here; it gained HBM share after launching a better-economics tester.
beginner_glossary.Merchant GPU test / fast-follower: Historically Teradyne was largely shut out of testing NVIDIA-style merchant GPUs (Advantest held it). In Q1 2026 Teradyne won its FIRST merchant-GPU production-test orders. Its 'fast-follower' plan is to convert more GPU device types onto its platform over a few years, aiming for a 30–70% dual-source share over the mid-term.
beginner_glossary.Custom ASIC test: Testing the in-house AI chips hyperscalers design (with Broadcom/Marvell). Teradyne already serves large ASIC programs; competing for more (incl. dual-source) is a key growth lever.
beginner_glossary.CPO / silicon photonics test (Photon 100: Co-packaged optics and silicon photonics move data with light instead of copper inside AI systems. Teradyne's new Photon 100 brings this testing 'from lab to fab.' Early days (~$100M in 2026) but a potential $300–700M/year mid-term market — and it tests the optics that AAOI/Lumentum/Coherent make.
beginner_glossary.Product Test / Omnyx: A smaller segment testing finished boards/assemblies (e.g. defense/aerospace, and now AI server boards via the new Omnyx platform, which catches defects 'plaguing the build-out of AI data centers').
beginner_glossary.Robotics (Universal Robots / MiR): Teradyne's industrial-robotics arm: Universal Robots (collaborative robot arms, 'cobots') and Mobile Industrial Robots (autonomous mobile robots, 'AMRs'). ~$91M/quarter, growing, increasingly used in AI data centers and 'physical AI.'
beginner_glossary.Wafer to AI data center: Teradyne's strategy of serving a customer's whole flow — from testing the wafer/chip, to testing the server board, to robots operating in the data center — for the big 'verticalized' AI companies.
beginner_glossary.Verticalization / VIP compute: The concentration of demand into a few huge vertically-integrated tech companies (hyperscalers, foundries, memory/networking giants). 'VIP' (vertically integrated production) compute = testing their custom AI silicon. Great for growth, but concentrates Teradyne's business into a few large programs.
beginner_glossary.Lumpy growth / limited visibility: Because demand is concentrated in a few large AI programs and a tester's lead time is short (~12–16 weeks, similar to the wafer itself, not the front-end tools), orders arrive late and unevenly. So Teradyne's revenue rises strongly over time but in uneven 'peaks and valleys' — and it can't see far beyond ~2 quarters.
beginner_glossary.Gross margin / operating margin: Percent of revenue left after direct costs (gross) and after all operating costs (operating). Teradyne hit records in Q1 2026 (60.9% gross, 37.5% operating) on peak AI volume and mix — but margins are 'lumpy' too and normalize when volume/mix shift.
beginner_glossary.Target model: Teradyne's stated MID-TERM financial goal: ~$6 billion revenue and $9.50–11 non-GAAP EPS. This is an aspiration the company is working toward (analysts model ~$4.5B revenue / ~$7.24 EPS for FY2026), not a current-year guide.
beginner_glossary.Duopoly (Advantest): The chip test-equipment market is essentially a two-player race between Teradyne and Japan's Advantest. Advantest is the larger leader (especially SoC/HBM); the two split most AI test demand.
beginner_glossary.P/E ratio (price-to-earnings): Share price ÷ yearly earnings per share. Teradyne trades ~75x trailing / ~56x forward (FY2026) earnings — a high multiple reflecting AI-test optimism on a business whose earnings are lumpy.
beginner_glossary.P/S ratio (price-to-sales): Market value ÷ yearly revenue. Teradyne is ~17x trailing sales — rich, reflecting the AI-test growth theme.

company_snapshot.what_it_is: Teradyne is a leading maker of automated test equipment (ATE) — the machines that test chips after manufacturing — and also owns an industrial-robotics business (Universal Robots, MiR). It is one half of the global chip-test duopoly with Japan's Advantest. AI has transformed it: AI-related demand was ~70% of Q1 2026 revenue, driving record results as it tests the compute, memory (HBM) and networking chips at the heart of AI. As of June 2026 it carries a ~$63B market cap.
company_snapshot.where_it_sits_in_the_chain: The back-end TEST equipment node. It SELLS testers to foundries (TSMC), OSATs (Amkor, ASE), memory makers (Micron/SK Hynix/Samsung), and hyperscalers/merchant-chip makers; its Photon 100 tests CPO/silicon-photonics (AAOI/Lumentum/Coherent), and its Robotics arm serves AI data centers. It competes head-to-head with Advantest. It is downstream of the chips and upstream of final assembly/data-center deployment.
company_snapshot.manufacturing_note: Teradyne is relatively capital-light — it designs testers and uses a multi-source contract-manufacturing strategy (more than doubled UltraFLEXplus shipments in 9 months while holding 12–16 week lead times). Growth is supplemented by M&A: recently the MultiLane Test JV (high-speed I/O / interconnect test) and the TestInsight acquisition (test-development software), ~$165M combined.

business_model.summary: Teradyne makes money mainly by selling automated test equipment to chipmakers and their packaging partners, plus a smaller robotics business. Because every advanced chip must be tested — and test intensity rises with complexity (HBM stacks, advanced packaging, CPO) — Teradyne rides AI chip volumes. Its 'wafer to AI data center' strategy widens its footprint from chip test to board test (Omnyx) to robots in the data center. The model delivers high margins (record ~61% gross, ~37% operating in Q1 2026) but LUMPY revenue, because demand concentrates in a few huge 'verticalized' AI customers and large device programs with short, late-arriving order cycles. Management's mid-term target is ~$6B revenue and $9.50–11 EPS.
how_they_make_money: Semiconductor Test (the engine): SoC (compute/AI) + Memory (HBM/DRAM) + IST. Q1 2026 $1.1B (broke $1B for the first time, +100%+ YoY) — SoC $882M (compute ~75%), Memory $203M, IST $27M.
Product Test: board/system test (defense/aerospace + new AI server-board platform Omnyx). $80M in Q1 2026 (+8% YoY).
Robotics: Universal Robots + MiR. $91M in Q1 2026 (+32% YoY), 4th straight sequential-growth quarter; AI/data-center use cases growing.
New TAMs: silicon photonics / CPO test (Photon 100, ~$100M in 2026 → $300–700M/yr mid-term); high-speed I/O test (MultiLane JV); test software (TestInsight).
Capital returns: small dividend ($0.52/yr) and de-minimis buybacks; cash is kept as 'dry powder' for M&A.
competitive_moat_analyst_view: Test duopoly: essentially only two credible suppliers of advanced ATE (Teradyne + Advantest) — high barriers (test IP, libraries, customer qualification). [analyst interpretation]
'Wafer to AI data center' breadth: SoC + memory + product/board test + robotics — a one-stop offering to verticalized AI giants that pure test peers can't match. [Q1 2026 call]

Incumbency + responsiveness: deep device libraries, multi-source manufacturing flexibility, and the ability to serve spot/quick-turn demand within lead time — a real advantage as customers prize supply resilience. [Q1 2026 call]
New-TAM optionality: Photon 100 (CPO/photonics), Omnyx (server boards), MultiLane (interconnect), TestInsight (software) extend the addressable market. [Q1 2026 call]
CAVEAT: the moat is real but the business is lumpy and concentrated, and Advantest is the larger leader in the prized SoC/HBM segments. [analyst interpretation]

revenue_streams.analyst_view: This is now overwhelmingly an AI test story: AI-related demand is ~70% of revenue, Semi Test broke $1B/quarter, and compute is ~75% of SoC (the business pivoted from mobile to AI). The growth engines are AI compute (with the first merchant-GPU win opening a multi-year 'fast-follower' share-gain path), HBM/memory test, and emerging CPO/photonics test (Photon 100). The defining caveat, stressed repeatedly by management, is LUMPINESS and CONCENTRATION: two specifying + one purchasing customer each >10% of revenue, demand tied to a few large ASIC/GPU programs, and visibility limited to ~2 quarters — so revenue grows strongly but unevenly, and a single program slip can move a quarter (or a year).

competitors.landscape_summary: Teradyne competes in a TWO-player global ATE duopoly with Japan's Advantest, which is the larger leader — especially in SoC and HBM test. The two split most AI test demand; share shifts at the margin when one launches a better-economics platform (as Teradyne did to gain HBM share, and as it now attempts in merchant GPU). Smaller/adjacent test players include Cohu (handlers/test) and various probe-card/handler specialists in the broader test cell. In Robotics, Teradyne's Universal Robots/MiR compete with other cobot/AMR makers. The key strategic dynamic is 'multi-sourcing': big AI customers increasingly want a second test-equipment source for supply resilience — a tailwind for Teradyne where Advantest is incumbent (and a risk where Teradyne is incumbent).

Advantest (its duopoly rival) is the obvious not-yet-covered counterpart.
competitors.differentiation_analyst_view: Teradyne differentiates on breadth ('wafer to data center': chip + board + robotics), incumbency with deep device libraries, and responsiveness/supply resilience — plus new-TAM platforms (Photon 100, Omnyx). But it is the #2 to Advantest in the most valuable SoC/HBM test, and its growth is lumpy and concentrated. Its biggest opportunity (merchant GPU, dual-sourcing) is also a reminder that share can move both ways — and customers' push for multi-sourcing cuts in Teradyne's favor where Advantest leads, but against it where Teradyne is the incumbent.

financial_performance.analyst_view: Financially this is a sharp AI-driven inflection: Q1 2026 revenue +87% with record ~61% gross and ~37.5% operating margins, and EPS up 241%. But three caveats are central: (1) LUMPINESS — management itself widened the H1 weighting range and stressed limited (~2-quarter) visibility, so quarters can swing on a single program; (2) some Q1 strength was non-recurring (one-time operational benefits, peak mix), with Q2 margins guided down to ~58–59%; and (3) the business is highly customer-concentrated. The trajectory toward the $6B / $9.50–11 target model is credible on the AI test waves, but the path will be uneven.

implied_multiples_analyst_view.interpretation: You are paying a growth multiple for an AI-test duopoly position. The bull case: the test TAM grows for years across the three AI waves, Teradyne gains GPU share and opens new TAMs (CPO/Omnyx), and earnings march to the $6B/$9.50–11 model — making ~42x FY2027 reasonable. The bear case: this is a lumpy, concentrated, #2-to-Advantest equipment business near its all-time high, where a high multiple leaves little room if AI capex digests or a key program slips.

valuation.analyst_view: Teradyne is a high-quality way to play AI test — a duopoly position, ~61% gross margins, a 'wafer to data center' footprint, the first merchant-GPU crack, and new TAMs (CPO/photonics, server-board, interconnect). But the valuation is demanding and the business is unusually lumpy: ~75x trailing / ~56x forward earnings, ~17x sales, near a 52-week high (~4.8x off the low), trading ABOVE the ~$375 consensus target, with management itself flagging limited visibility and concentration. The honest read: real AI-test growth and credible mid-term upside (the $6B model), but priced for it — with the wide $270–$470 target range capturing how much the uneven, customer-concentrated revenue cadence clouds the picture.

Customers' push for second sources helps Teradyne where Advantest leads, but exposes Teradyne's own incumbent positions to share loss.
Robotics is improving but management remains cautious about extrapolating growth; it is a smaller, separate market with its own dynamics.
Test equipment is globally exposed (customers and partners across Taiwan, Japan, Korea, China, Israel); trade/export actions are swing factors.

final_research_summary.one_paragraph: Teradyne (TER) is one half of the global chip TEST-equipment duopoly (with Japan's Advantest) — it makes the automated test equipment that verifies AI chips after manufacturing — plus an industrial-robotics arm (Universal Robots, MiR). AI has transformed it: AI-related demand was ~70% of Q1 2026 revenue (up from ~60%), and its 'wafer to AI data center' strategy spans testing compute/SoC (GPUs, ASICs), HBM/DRAM memory, and networking, extending into server-board test (Omnyx) and silicon-photonics/CPO test (the new Photon 100). Q1 2026 (reported 2026-04-29) was an all-time record: revenue $1.282B (+87% YoY), non-GAAP EPS $2.56 (+241%), record 60.9% gross and 37.5% operating margins, with Semiconductor Test breaking $1B in a quarter for the first time (SoC $882M, compute ~75%; Memory $203M) and Robotics +32% YoY (4th straight sequential gain) — and Teradyne won its FIRST merchant-GPU production-test orders, opening a multi-year share-gain path. The defining feature, stressed by management, is LUMPINESS and CONCENTRATION: two specifying plus one purchasing customer each >10% of revenue, demand tied to a few large programs, and visibility limited to ~2 quarters, so revenue grows strongly but unevenly (Q2 is guided to $1.15–1.25B with margins normalizing to ~58–59% after one-time Q1 benefits). FY2025 revenue was $3.19B (+13%); the mid-term target model is ~$6B revenue / $9.50–11 EPS (analysts model ~$4.48B / ~$7.24 for FY2026, then ~$9.50 in FY2027). On valuation, the stock (~$403; ~$63B market cap; ~75x trailing / ~56x forward FY2026 earnings; ~17x sales) has risen ~4.8x off its 52-week low, trades near its high, and sits ABOVE the ~$375 'Buy' consensus target — with a wide $270–$470 range reflecting the lumpy-visibility uncertainty. The honest read: a high-quality AI-test duopoly with real growth (GPU crack, HBM test, new CPO/photonics and board-test TAMs) and credible mid-term upside, but priced for it — a #2-to-Advantest, customer-concentrated, lumpy capital-equipment business near its highs, where timing and concentration, not the secular thesis, are the swing factors.
